commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[eval] Keep policy records where EvalDash catalogs them (#10965)

Reject a policy launch (one with `--policy-finalization-config`) whose
remote records prefix is not
exactly `gs://marin-eval-metadata/evals` or
`s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals`, the roots EvalDash
catalogs, or whose `--resume-results-path` is not a
`<root>/<run_id>/results` directory under them.
EvalDash discovers only `<root>/<run_id>/record.json`, so records in
another bucket or under a nested
prefix such as `evals/ablations/<replay>/` never appear on the
dashboard. A local path is still
accepted for dry runs and tests. The Snowball v0.1 sampling
re-evaluation wrote 26 policy runs to
`s3://marin-rno2a/marin/evals`, which EvalDash does not scan, so none
appeared until they were copied.

The campaign README now says to launch policy evaluations from the
revisions pinned in #10197, not
from `main`, and that nested replay outputs are not EvalDash runs. The
directory on `main` differs
from the policy; for example, its SWE-bench budget is 32,768 tokens and
the policy runs 131,072.
The guard reaches the policy launcher only once a later policy pins a
revision that contains it.
Grader-replay promotion tools are unchanged and can still link nested
replay outputs in a tracker.

Part of #10197

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[eval] Grade first valid CruxEval answer span (#10970)

CruxEval now grades the first `[ANSWER]...[/ANSWER]` span that holds a
candidate answer, not the first span. For input prediction the span must
contain an `f(...)` call; for output prediction the extracted literal
must parse as a Python expression. If no span qualifies, the first span
is graded as before.

Models served without a reasoning parser emit their reasoning as
content. That reasoning often restates the prompt's instruction to use
"[ANSWER] and [/ANSWER] tags", so the old grader extracted the literal
`and`. The item then failed with a `NameError`, even when a correct
assertion followed. Taking the last span instead was worse: models often
append further example assertions, and on Snowball v0.1 that rule
regressed 50 items.

On the saved Snowball v0.1 CruxEval responses (T=0.6 re-evaluation), 78
input-prediction items extracted `and`. Under the fix, 75 of them select
a later answer and 62 of those now pass. Input accuracy rises from 0.714
to 0.791; output prediction (0.790) is unchanged, and no previously
passing item changes. Models served with reasoning parsers, such as
Qwen3.6 and Gemma 4, had no `and` extractions.

The same selection now applies in the canonical TaskCompendium CruxEval
grader, so #10957 can remove vendor/evalchemy without losing the
correction.

Existing policy #10197 cells are not regraded. This changes grading for
future runs only.

Part of #10197

---------

Co-authored-by: Ben Feuer <benfeuer@Bens-MacBook-Pro.local>

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[levanter] Preserve reference generation settings during HF export (#10798)

Preserve the pinned reference model's `generation_config.json` during HF
checkpoint export unless the caller supplies an explicit override.
Previously, exports could silently omit secondary EOS tokens and other
generation defaults, changing stopping behavior at evaluation time. Copy
the complete file for local, object-store, and Hub references; tolerate
a missing optional file, while propagating authentication and other read
errors.

The offline integration fixture supplies its local tokenizer's EOS token
explicitly, so its export does not require an uncached Hub file.

commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[harbor] Convert Pi session logs to ATIF trajectories (#10972)

[harbor] Convert Pi session logs to ATIF trajectories

Pi wrote only its raw session JSONL (pi.txt), so Harbor archived no
trajectory for Pi policies and EvalDash showed no episode viewer for
BFCL and BixBench runs. populate_context_post_run now converts the
pi.txt event stream into the standard ATIF trajectory.json beside it,
which Harbor's archive step already persists and EvalDash already
renders. message_end events map to ATIF steps: assistant turns carry
their tool calls and usage metrics, tool results attach to the
preceding step as observation results, and user and system turns
become steps. Streaming deltas and duplicate tool-execution events
are skipped. A malformed or truncated stream yields a partial
trajectory or none and never fails the trial.

Existing runs stay trace-less; only new Pi runs produce trajectories.
New BFCL and BixBench Pi runs will show episode trajectories in
EvalDash. The tau3 ACP runner keeps its own event format and is
unaffected.

---------

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
Strengthen holistic reviews of design and contract boundaries (#11011)

Strengthen holistic review of responsibility, cohesion, abstraction, and
shared contracts. A change can pass local tests while scattering one
behavior across unrelated modules, duplicating existing concepts, or
letting producers and consumers interpret the same data differently.
Require structural findings to explain the consequence and give a
concrete replacement supported by code or a reproduction.

Check whether fakes bypass the contract under review and whether tests
and documentation answer callers' actual questions. The Loom launch
prompt and profile invoke these design questions within the existing
review. Posting, finding numbers, telemetry, and re-review behavior are
unchanged.

---------

Co-authored-by: rjpower <rjpower@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: asartran
commits.message:
[haliax] Use plgpu.dot in the Pallas-Triton ragged_dot kernels (#11051)

Call `plgpu.dot` instead of `pl.dot` in haliax's Pallas-Triton
`ragged_dot` kernels, so they still compile on JAX 0.12, which removed
`pl.dot`.

On JAX 0.12, any call into these kernels fails while tracing with
`AttributeError: pl.dot was deprecated in JAX v0.11.0, and removed in
JAX v0.12.0`. Grug's ragged all-to-all MoE path on AMD GPUs uses them,
so that path stops working before it launches any kernel.

`plgpu.dot` (`jax.experimental.pallas.triton.dot`) has the same
signature as `pl.dot` (`a, b, trans_a, trans_b, allow_tf32, precision`)
on both 0.11.1 and 0.12.0. On the Triton backend, `pl.dot` already
dispatched to it, so nothing changes on JAX 0.11. Grug's AMD Pallas
flash kernel already calls `plgpu.dot`.

On 8x MI355X with jax 0.12.0, the ragged all-to-all MoE forward pass and
its gradients matched a dense JAX reference within 7e-7 relative error
in 3 of 3 runs. This branch is independent of #11046, which allows JAX
0.12, and can merge first.

Co-authored-by: Amy Sartran <users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: dlwh
commits.message:
[levanter] Keep fused cross entropy correct with tensor parallelism (#11028)

Compute fused cross entropy with complete vocabulary and contraction
dimensions while retaining per-example sharding. The local kernel
receives global target IDs, so partitioning its vocabulary made losses
and gradients incorrect. In a four-H100 run with a 16,384-token
vocabulary, every scored target at or above the local width of 4,096
produced an infinite loss.

Multi-device regressions compare per-position and reduced losses,
gradients of hidden activations and language-model-head weights, z-loss,
soft caps, shifted targets, and global argmax against an independent
full-vocabulary reference. The fix replicates the vocabulary and
contraction axes at the local loss-kernel boundary. Its performance cost
relative to a correct vocabulary-parallel implementation remains
unmeasured.

commits.author: ravwojdyla-agent
commits.message:
[zephyr] Retry a shared pool's failed start (#11012)

A shared Zephyr pool now retries a failed start on a fresh coordinator,
with the same `max_execution_retries` budget and backoff as a dedicated
pipeline. Before, a shared pool started once, outside any retry loop, so
one coordinator that missed the 900-second readiness limit failed every
step that used the pool.

On 2026-11-02, the Datakit tier 1 canary hit this in
https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/41481663945. The
normalize pipeline's dedicated coordinator and the shared pool's
coordinator both missed the limit while installing dependencies. The
dedicated pipeline passed on a retry; the shared pool failed the run.

A retry does not help if coordinator setup regularly takes longer than
15 minutes. In that case the readiness limit itself has to go up. This
replaces #10853, which raised the limit to 30 minutes for the Datakit
shared coordinator only.

Part of #10848

---------
